message.content:
The area of the original square is \(49\), so its side length is

\[
\sqrt{49}=7
\]

Folding the square so that one pair of opposite corners coincide creates a crease along the other diagonal. Unfolding divides the square into two congruent right isosceles triangles.

Each triangle has:

- two legs of length \(7\)
- hypotenuse equal to the diagonal of the square:

\[
7\sqrt{2}
\]

So the perimeter of one triangle is

\[
7+7+7\sqrt{2}=14+7\sqrt{2}
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{14+7\sqrt{2}}\).
